newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH FIN MIN '97 FORECAST REALISTIC -KKK'S KERO.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH FIN MIN '97 FORECAST REALISTIC -KKK'S KERO.

text.p: The Finnish finance ministry's economic forecast for 1997 is quite realistic, Central Chamber of Commerce (KKK) economist Jukka Kero wrote in the KKK's Kauppakamari newletter received on Wednesday.
On February 18, the finance ministry's economics department upped its 1997 GDP growth forecast to 4.6 percent from a 3.9 percent growth forecast last September.
"The finance ministry's forecast can be regarded as quite realistic based on information currently at hand," Kero said.
Conditions were favourable with demand on the rise, debt in decline, interest rates low and confidence strong, he said.
"Investments remain the biggest domestic uncertainty factor," Kero said, noting surveys made by industry lobbies did not point to any growth in 1997 industrial investment.

But he added that industrial investment accounted for less than a quarter of total investment, and that investment growth -- projected by the finance ministry at 10.8 percent this year -- would largely depend on investment by service industries and in construction.
The stronger dollar was supporting economic growth in EU countries, but that was insufficient to revive on its own private consumption and building activity in Europe, Kero said.
